source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible v1 source studies homoscedastic cyclic graphs, gives sufficient generic distinguishability conditions for subclasses, and states that it conjectures a strengthening for more noncomplete graphs.
The half-trek criterion is a sufficient generic-identifiability condition, polynomially checkable, and does not require an acyclic directed part.

The paper treats cyclic and acyclic linear Gaussian directed graphs, defines distribution equivalence and quasi-equivalence, and provides analytic, graphical, and score-based structure-learning methods.
The paper establishes expected dimension for simple cyclic linear models and motivates score-based structure learning; it does not state the proposed homoscedastic SCC Hall criterion.
The paper identifies equal-variance DAG structure through an ordering of conditional variances and develops a covariance-based causal-discovery procedure.
